messages:
emma_support: FYI escalation from Acme integration team — their service is failing to parse our JSON-mode output, getting a JS error: "Unexpected token \\ in JSON at position 14". They say it worked last week and started failing after a small model update.

acme_integration: We see the response body wrapped as a JSON string (double-encoded). Example from our logs:
```json
{
  "id": "resp_123",
  "content": "{\"user\":\"Alice\",\"note\":\"Line1\\nLine2\"}"
}
```
This breaks our parser (we call JSON.parse on content).

alex_engineer: Thanks — can you paste the raw bytes / content-type and whether you used streaming? Also, did you request structured output via the API param or via a system prompt?

acme_integration: We used the JSON-mode param: `response_format": "json"` and streaming=false. Content-Type is `application/json; charset=utf-8`. No proxies in between besides our app.

maya_sre: Quick check: did they send the response through any logging that might double-escape? Sometimes middleware does stringification.

acme_integration: We logged the exact response body from the HTTP client before any processing. Here's a hex snippet and length if that helps: `0x7b226964...` length 482 bytes. We see backslashes in the content field itself.

luis_infra: Two hypotheses: (1) model returned a JSON string literal (i.e., included surrounding quotes), so we return a JSON containing a string with embedded escapes; (2) our structured-output wrapper inadvertently stringified the model's JSON object before emitting. We rolled a small runtime patch last week that touched streaming chunk assembly — could be related.

emma_support: Also customer reported a latency spike around the same time as the failures — average 120ms -> 600ms during the window. They hit our hosted API. No billing anomalies on their account. They briefly saw auth 401s earlier but that was due to a rotated API key on their side, not ours (they confirmed reissue).

alex_engineer: Can you repro locally with their prompt + params? If we can reproduce with our curl/SDK we can rule out their client.

emma_support: Repro steps provided by Acme (they want us to run this exact call):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "redwood-2.1",
    "response_format": "json",
    "temperature": 0,
    "prompt": "You are a JSON-only assistant. Output a single JSON object with fields: user, note. user: string, note: string with possible newlines. Do not wrap output in code fences or extra text."
  }'
```

deploy-bot: deploy event: eng-runtime/streaming-assembler v2026.03.10 rolled at 2026-03-08T02:14:00Z affecting canary and prod.

alex_engineer: Good find. I'll try reproducing against canary and prod. If we see double-encoded content on canary it's almost certainly a regression in the assembler.

maya_sre: On the latency point — streaming assembler changes might increase head-of-line latency for small requests. If assembler delays until buffer threshold is hit, smaller payloads could be wrapped/escaped differently when reassembled; I/O code paths might call `JSON.stringify` defensively.

luis_infra: Quick internal check: runtime logs show one request with id req_987 that had `emitChunk` fallback triggered, and assembler used fallback path that calls `stringify()` on chunk payloads. That path was supposed to only meta-wrap chunks, but could have been applied to final content.

emma_support: Acme can confirm this sample output from our API (raw):
```json
{"id":"resp_123","choices":[{"content":"{\"user\":\"Alice\",\"note\":\"Line1\\nLine2\"}","finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{}}
```
They expect the content field to be an object, not a JSON-encoded string.

alex_engineer: Root cause likely: assembler fallback invoked `JSON.stringify` on an already-serialized JSON object, resulting in double-encoding of quotes and newlines (\n -> \\n in the outer JSON). Fix: ensure final payload emits native JSON objects rather than stringified JSON in the `content` slot. I'll prepare a patch to bypass stringify on final aggregation and add unit tests for structured-output path.

acme_integration: Any temporary workaround we can use while you patch?

emma_support: Workarounds: (1) client-side: if you detect content is a string, `JSON.parse(content)` once to get the object (safe if you know the field), (2) use non-streaming and set `response_format` but also include an explicit system prompt: "OUTPUT RAW JSON OBJECT WITHOUT SURROUNDING QUOTES" — might coax model to emit object tokens instead of string. Not ideal.

maya_sre: I'll also roll a canary fix to revert the assembler fallback for small payloads to see if that clears customer failures and latency.

alex_engineer: I'll open PR + QA. Tagging this as P1 for correctness of structured output.

emma_support: Updated Acme: we've identified a server-side regression in the streaming assembly path that can double-encode structured responses. We're patching now; expected canary fix within 2 hours, prod rollback/patch within 6 hours. For immediate parsing, please try a client-side `if (typeof content === 'string') content = JSON.parse(content);`.

acme_integration: Thanks, will try the parse workaround and confirm. Appreciate the quick triage.

emma_support: Follow-ups: Alex will post a link to PR and QA notes once available. Maya will confirm canary results. Luis will monitor for any billing/traffic anomalies (none expected).

alex_engineer: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/1427 — fix replaces stringify with direct object merge and adds test for newline handling in structured output.

maya_sre: Canary result: verified fix on canary, small sample set now returning object in `content` field. Rolling to prod in 30m.

acme_integration: Confirmed our test run with the parse workaround passes and after canary patch our integration no longer sees escaped newlines. All good here so far.

emma_support: Closing loop with customer and marking thread resolved after prod patch. If anyone wants postmortem notes, I'll collect telemetry (latency window, affected model versions, deploy id).

luis_infra: Postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause (streaming assembler stringify fallback), customer impact, rollback/patch, tests added, monitoring alert to detect double-encoded content.

emma_support: Thanks team :thumbsup:
